name: Imani

biography.name: Imani

background.family: Lives with parents and a younger brother.
background.finances: Stable moderate income; family favors restrained future spending.
background.cultureLanguages: English; grandparents share gardening stories and local history.
background.school: Public high school with science club and art electives.
background.accessOpportunities: Supervised pond observations and school displays; no laboratory or studio work experience.

timeline.story: In 2014, Imani liked watching puddles change after rain and drawing creatures that supposedly lived in them. She also enjoyed building blanket forts, usually filling them with books rather than acting out elaborate adventures.

At six, she began school nature walks and asked why some insects appeared near water. During 2017, she drew what she saw, sometimes adding imagined details until a teacher helped distinguish observation from invention.

In 2018, Imani made short stories about garden animals with her brother. She liked explaining real features through fictional characters, while learning that a funny detail could accidentally make another child misunderstand what the animal actually did.

During 2020, she kept a small notebook of outdoor observations near home and tried several ways to illustrate them. She missed hearing people ask questions about her drawings and began sharing pages with a few classmates online.

At twelve, Imani joined supervised pond observations through a club. In 2023, she helped prepare a science-fair poster and discovered that the most satisfying moments came when visitors understood a relationship they had previously found confusing.

Across 2024 and 2025, she revised diagrams and short explanatory stories after readers misunderstood them. Patient care did not attract her; she remained interested in both living systems and the creative work of making an explanation easier to follow.

At sixteen in 2026, Imani is comparing Texas degree programs and introductory workshops without choosing one professional identity. She wants moderate expenses and room for both science and creative work, knowing she has experienced neither a research laboratory nor a design studio.

avoids: Pressure to choose only science or art
ambitions: Compare study combining or accommodating both interests
She imagines a modest home with outdoor access and time to keep observing and making things.

biography.selfDescription: I liked the science fair most when somebody stopped looking puzzled. I want to understand what is happening in a pond, and I also want to find a good way to show it without pretending one interest cancels the other.
openQuestions: Will laboratory routines appeal as much as field observations?
How does she respond to extended creative critique?
